title: When Somebody Starts Winning
tagline: Success doesn’t only reveal the person receiving it. It reveals everybody standing nearby.
headline: When Somebody Starts Winning
headline_sub: Comparison, Envy and Celebrating Someone Else’s Success
seo_title: When a Teammate’s Success Feels Like a Threat | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Success reveals everybody standing nearby. What Saul and David teach about comparison, envy and keeping success from reorganizing a team.

scriptures.text: “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.” “Saul was very angry; this refrain displeased him greatly….” “And from that time on Saul kept a close eye on David.”

blocks.text: DAVID’S SUCCESS CHANGED SAUL’S INTERPRETATION OF DAVID.
The song enters the room:

items: and David his tens of thousands.”

blocks.text: And Scripture says:
“Saul kept a close eye on David.”
The battle began long before Saul threw the spear.

steps: Their success becomes commentary about me.
Their blessing begins feeling like my threat.

blocks.text: That is:
THE BATTLE BEFORE THE SPEAR.
Saul’s hand eventually threw what comparison had already been sharpening inside him.
“THERE IS LESS FOR ME BECAUSE THERE IS MORE FOR HIM.”

items: Now his increase feels like my decrease.

blocks.text: And slowly:
I STOP WATCHING TO CHEER HIM ON.
I START WATCHING TO MEASURE MYSELF.
That’s exactly what happened to Saul.
Romans 12 says:
“Rejoice with those who rejoice.”

items: That’s much harder than it sounds.
Especially when someone receives something you wanted.
Rejoicing becomes an act of surrender.

blocks.text: It says:
“YOUR SUCCESS DOES NOT THREATEN MY ASSIGNMENT.”
God’s calling on another man’s life does not cancel God’s calling on mine.

items: His opportunity does not make me invisible.
His platform does not reduce my worth.
His income does not determine mine.
His recognition does not determine my significance.

blocks.text: I can celebrate him because:
I DON’T NEED HIS STORY TO BECOME SMALLER FOR MINE TO MATTER.

items: But success also tests the successful man.
Will everyone become afraid to challenge him?
The successful person becomes the gravitational center.

blocks.text: A HEALTHY BROTHERHOOD DOESN’T BECOME A COURT BECAUSE ONE MAN BECAME A KING.
Christ remains Lord of the room.

items: WHOSE SUCCESS CHANGES HOW I SEE THEM?
WHO HAVE I STARTED WATCHING INSTEAD OF CELEBRATING?
WHAT DOES THEIR SUCCESS MAKE ME FEAR ABOUT MYSELF?

blocks.text: And if you’re succeeding:

items: CAN THE SAME BROTHERS STILL CORRECT ME?
HAVE I BECOME HARDER TO CHALLENGE?
HAS SUCCESS CHANGED WHAT I EXPECT FROM THE ROOM?

blocks.text: Then ask:
CAN SUCCESS ENTER THIS ROOM WITHOUT BECOMING LORD OF IT?
Celebrate someone whose success has been difficult for you.

items: Bring the envy to God first.
Then honor what is genuinely honorable.

blocks.text: YOU DON’T NEED HIS LANE.
YOU NEED FAITHFULNESS IN YOURS.
The battle began long before Saul threw the spear.
Keep another man’s success from becoming my insecurity.
Teach me to celebrate without measuring myself.
And when You entrust success to me, keep me humble, teachable, and accountable.
Don’t let success reorganize our brotherhood around status.
Jesus remains Lord of the room.
The battle began long before Saul threw the spear.
Saul’s hand eventually threw what comparison had already been sharpening inside him.
I don’t need his story to become smaller for mine to matter.
Your success does not threaten my assignment.
A healthy brotherhood doesn’t become a court because one man became a king.
-TheWrkShop
